thread.title: Apple Bears Come Out For iPhone Maker's Second-Quarter Report

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Bears Come Out For iPhone Maker's Second-Quarter Report
text:
Wall Street has soured on Apple ( AAPL ) ahead of the consumer electronics giant's March-quarter earnings report, due after the market close Tuesday.
X Investment bank Barclays on Monday cut its price target on Apple stock to 157 from 168 and reiterated its equal-weight rating.
Shares gained 1.8% to close at 165.26 on the stock market today , on word the company may repatriate $285 billion in cash to the U.S. and buy back more stock. But the company has been a stock market laggard of late compared with the S&P 500.
Analysts are increasingly negative about its prospects amid reports of slowing iPhone sales.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The "softening iPhone franchise is a big problem," Barclays analyst Mark Moskowitz said in a note to clients. Apple likely alienated many users with higher prices for its new iPhones, including the iPhone X, which starts at $999, he said.
He sees average selling prices for iPhones and rival handsets coming down because "end users only care about battery life, camera and texting."
Apple Could Guide Lower BMO Capital Markets analyst Tim Long expects the tech icon to guide expectations lower for the June quarter. He reiterated his market-perform rating and price target of 166 on Apple stock in his report to clients Sunday.
"We believe Apple will guide down on weaker iPhone expectations," Long said. "We believe price elasticity and lengthening smartphone replacement cycles are mostly to blame, and we do not expect the issue to be solved by the next cycle."
Long cut his earnings estimates for the current fiscal year and next. He also lowered his iPhone sales expectations for this year and next.
"We believe price elasticity is affecting the current cycle, as new models introduced cost, on average, over $100 more than last year's new models," he said. "Additionally, we believe consumers are satisfied to hold onto their smartphones longer. Although we estimate iPhones get replaced more frequently than competitors' phones, we believe replacement rates will continue to worsen."
Consensus Estimates Analysts now expect earnings of $2.69 a share in the March quarter on sales of $61.1 billion, according to Zacks Investment Research. Wall Street sees the company selling 53 million iPhone units in the quarter.
Analysts say Apple should boost its capital return plan with its second-quarter report thanks to repatriated foreign profits. But the higher share buybacks and dividends are priced into the stock, analysts say.
For the June quarter, analysts expect earnings of $2.11 a share on sales of $51.6 billion. They're looking for Apple to sell 42 million iPhone units.
Oppenheimer analyst Andrew Uerkwitz cut his sales and earnings estimates for Apple for the next two years. He reiterated his perform rating on Apple stock in a report Sunday.
"We believe there is a lengthening of the replacement cycle and diminishing utility of high-end phones across markets, to which Apple is not immune," Uerkwitz said. "As long as iPhone sales do not grow, we believe the stock will struggle to work."
